scenes.text: In the year 300, a Roman soldier could be paid a pile of coins, and still go hungry. How did the richest empire on Earth go broke?
Under Emperor Augustus, the silver denarius was almost pure silver. But empires are expensive. Legions. Roads. Free bread for Rome.
When money ran short, emperors found a shortcut. Melt the coins, mix in cheaper metal, and mint more of them.
Nero trimmed a little. Later emperors trimmed a lot. By the 270s, the silver coin was mostly bronze. Under five percent silver.
Prices soared. In 301, Emperor Diocletian tried to fix prices by law, with death as the penalty. It failed.
Rome didn't just run out of money. It made too much of it. Sound familiar?
